title: Mica chrome, rounded corners, theme / DPI / text size
setup: Use a colourful desktop wallpaper so Mica tint is visible.
The wizard captures the app's [s4] diagnostics line automatically; press l during a test to view it.
Note your GPU vendor (the wizard records it).

tests.title: Default launch: Mica on chrome, opaque cards
tests.do: Keep the window active over the wallpaper. Take a screenshot (press c).
tests.expect: Header, tab bar and footer show MICA (subtle wallpaper tint); the card zone is opaque warm off-white. 8px rounded corners, DWM shadow, 1px grey border. Diagnostics show 'chrome: Backdrop(Mica)' and 'DWM: dark=ok corners=ok border=ok extend=Full:ok backdrop=2:ok'. FAILURE MODES to record: black chrome, opaque grey/white chrome, a 1px dark line along the top edge.

tests.title: Same with the software renderer
tests.do: Look at the chrome again. Take a screenshot (press c).
tests.expect: Same as test 1. This decides which renderer we use.

tests.title: Drag and resize
tests.do: Drag the window by the header across the wallpaper. Resize from the left edge, right edge, bottom edge and bottom-right corner.
tests.expect: The tint updates with position; dragging and resizing work. Width stays within 260 to 480.

tests.title: Inactive window turns flat
tests.do: Click another app so the panel becomes inactive, then click back on the panel.
tests.expect: Inactive: chrome goes FLAT neutral (expected Mica behaviour). Active again: tint returns.

tests.title: Never-activating window (the real panel's situation)
tests.do: Click inside the panel.
tests.expect: Record whether the chrome is ever tinted (expected: flat, since the window never activates).

tests.title: Workaround: keep-active look
tests.do: Click inside the panel. Look at the chrome, corners and shadow.
tests.expect: Record whether the tint appears, and whether corners and shadow survive with WS_EX_TOOLWINDOW. This decides the panel material.

tests.title: Live dark / light switching
tests.do: While running: Settings > Personalization > Colors > Choose your mode > Dark, then back to Light.
tests.expect: Within about 1 s the card zone turns near-black, cards dark, text light, and Mica turns dark ('dark=ok'). Diagnostics name the trigger and 'theme dark'. Reverses cleanly.

tests.title: Transparency effects off / on
tests.do: Settings > Personalization > Colors > Transparency effects: off, then on.
tests.expect: Off: chrome becomes solid and matches the card zone, 'chrome: Solid(TransparencyOff)', 'backdrop=1:ok', hairlines still separate the zones. On: Mica returns.

tests.title: High contrast theme
tests.do: Turn on a contrast theme (Settings > Accessibility > Contrast themes > for example Night sky), then turn it off.
tests.expect: On: every surface uses the theme window colour, text uses its text colour, 1px borders in the text colour on cards and around the window, solid chrome, 'chrome: Solid(HighContrast)'. Off: the normal theme returns.

tests.title: Per-monitor DPI
tests.do: With two monitors at different scales (for example 100% and 150%) drag the window between them. Also change Settings > Display > Scale while it runs. (One monitor only? change the scale and mark pass if it behaves.)
tests.expect: The window keeps its logical size (320 px wide by default), text stays sharp, 'DPI scale' updates in the diagnostics, corners and shadow persist.

tests.title: Windows Text size setting
tests.do: Settings > Accessibility > Text size > 150% > Apply. Then 225%, then back to 100%.
tests.expect: Text grows and the header, tabs and footer grow with it ('text scale 1.50' / '2.25'). RECORD WHICH SIGNAL triggered the refresh. Known: at 175% and above the tab bar overflows (the real ListTabBar must scroll).

tests.title: Matrix: extend frame 1px
tests.do: Look at the chrome. Record: Mica visible? shadow? rounded corners? a top 1px line?
tests.expect: Expected: opaque chrome.

tests.title: Matrix: no frame extension
tests.do: Same observations.
tests.expect: Expected: opaque chrome.

tests.title: Matrix: shadow off
tests.do: Same observations.
tests.expect: Record whether the shadow is gone.

tests.title: Matrix: shadow off, full extension
tests.do: Same observations.
tests.expect: Shadow comes from either S4_SHADOW=1 or the frame extension.

tests.title: Matrix: Mica Alt
tests.do: Same observations.
tests.expect: Record how it differs from plain Mica.

tests.title: Matrix: Acrylic
tests.do: Same observations.
tests.expect: Record how it differs (we do not plan to use it).

tests.title: No white flash in dark mode
tests.do: Switch Windows to dark mode, then press r (relaunch) five times, watching the first frame each time.
tests.expect: No white or light flash before the dark UI appears. Record any flash.

tests.title: Resize strips
tests.do: Resize quickly from the right edge back and forth.
tests.expect: Record any black or transparent strips during resize. Compare the two renderers (test 2).

tests.title: Readability on strong wallpapers
tests.do: Use a saturated dark wallpaper in light mode, then a saturated light wallpaper in dark mode. Zoom the footer with Magnifier (Win and Plus).
tests.expect: Footer text is readable, with no coloured fringes or halos around glyphs.

tests.title: Battery saver
tests.do: (Laptop) Turn on Energy saver / Battery saver.
tests.expect: Record whether Mica goes flat and whether 'transparency' in the diagnostics changes.

tests.title: NVIDIA OpenGL compatibility (only if test 1 was black)
tests.do: NVIDIA Control Panel > Manage 3D settings > OpenGL GDI compatibility > Prefer compatibility, then repeat test 1.
tests.expect: Record whether that fixes the default renderer. Informational only.

tests.title: Fallback look (forced solid chrome)
tests.do: Look at the window and compare it with DESIGN.md. Take a screenshot (press c).
tests.expect: 'Solid(ForcedByConfig)', 'backdrop=1:ok'. Corners, shadow and border stay.

tests.title: Windows 10: solid chrome
tests.do: Look at the window (default renderer).
tests.expect: Solid chrome, 'chrome: Solid(UnsupportedOs)', SQUARE corners, a DWM shadow, a Slint-drawn 1px border. No black areas. The 'dark=' entry may show an error code on older builds (harmless).

tests.title: Windows 10: software renderer
tests.do: Look at the window.
tests.expect: Same as W1.

tests.title: Windows 10: drag and resize
tests.do: Drag and resize the window.
tests.expect: Works.

tests.title: Windows 10: dark / light switching
tests.do: Settings > Personalization > Colors > default app mode Dark, then Light, while running.
tests.expect: Tokens switch within about 1 s and the diagnostics show the trigger.

tests.title: Windows 10: Make text bigger
tests.do: Settings > Ease of Access > Display > Make text bigger > 150%.
tests.expect: Text and chrome grow. Record which signal arrived.

tests.title: Windows 10: high contrast
tests.do: Toggle high contrast (Left Alt + Left Shift + Print Screen).
tests.expect: System colours are used, solid chrome, 1px text-colour borders.

tests.title: Windows 10: two monitors / scaling
tests.do: Drag between monitors at different scales, or change Display > Scale while running.
tests.expect: Logical size kept, text sharp, 'DPI scale' updates.

tests.title: Windows 10: no 'entry point not found' dialog
tests.do: Relaunch the app (r) and watch start-up.
tests.expect: No error dialog about SetWindowSubclass / comctl32.
